question.problem:
Environmental scientists are studying the population of fish in a lake.
They observe that the fish population increases due to reproduction at a rate $r(t)$ given by the function

$$
r(t)=40{t}^{2}+6t,
$$

where $r(t)$ is measured in fish per month, and $t>0$ is the time in months since the study began.
At the same time, $10$ fish are lost each month due to predation.

If there were initially $500$ fish in the lake, find the expression that gives $P(t),$ the number of fish in the lake $t$ months after the beginning of the study.

$P(t)=\frac{40}{3}{t}^{3}\,+$

{{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
The population of the lake is increasing at a rate of $r(t)$ fish per month and is decreasing at a rate of $10$ fish per month. Therefore, the **rate of change** $R(t)$ of the number of fish is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(t) & =r(t)-10 \\  & =40{t}^{2}+6t-10.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the total number $P(t)$ of fish after $t$ months, we apply the second fundamental theorem of calculus:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t) & =P(0)+{\int }_{0}^{t}R(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =500+{\int }_{0}^{t}(40{x}^{2}+6x-10)\,\text{d}x\end{aligned}
$$

To ensure that our final function is a function of $t$ only, we use a different variable ($x$) for the integration.

We can simplify the expression as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(t) & =500+{\int }_{0}^{t}40{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{0}^{t}6x\,\text{d}x-{\int }_{0}^{t}10\,\text{d}x \\  & =500+{40\,\frac{{x}^{3}}{3}|}_{0}^{t}+{6\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}|}_{0}^{t}-10x{|}_{0}^{t} \\  & =500+\frac{40}{3}{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}-10t \\  & =\frac{40}{3}{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}-10t+500\end{aligned}
$$
